name: Abū Isḥāq Ibrāhīm ibn Sufyān al-Ziyādī
summary: Basran grammarian of the line of Ziyād ibn Abīhi, pupil of al-Aṣmaʿī and teacher of al-Mubarrad, who read Sībawayh's Book and left remarks on it that al-Sīrāfī cites.
bio: Al-Ziyādī was named after his ancestor Ziyād ibn Sumayya. He took from al-Aṣmaʿī and others, and al-Mubarrad took from him. He read the Book of Sībawayh and left remarks on it and disagreements with it, which al-Sīrāfī cites in his commentary on the Book.

Ibn al-Anbārī names his books on proverbs, on the dots and vowel signs, and Tanmīq al-akhbār. Al-Zubaydī counts him in the seventh generation of the grammarians of Basra. Ibn al-Anbārī gives no year of his death.

sources.title: Ibn al-Anbārī, Nuzhat al-alibbāʾ fī ṭabaqāt al-udabāʾ (Cairo 1294/1877), pp. 269
